name: human_at_budget
_comment: Reproduces the 2026-08-26 dead end. The Developer never converges, so the Arbiter is called twice INSIDE the loop and both times decides on its own (REVIEWER_IS_RIGHT) - neither of those rulings may swallow a pending --human-answer. The dispute survives to the iteration budget (max_iterations=10). Without --human-answer the tail arbiter returns NEEDS_HUMAN_DECISION and the run PAUSES (AWAITING_HUMAN). With --human-answer the answer outranks the arbiter at that stop point, is applied as the binding ruling, and buys human_resume_iterations extra iterations - the Developer then returns FEASIBLE and the Tech Lead READY_FOR_HUMAN_REVIEW -> PASS. Before the fix this scenario paused in BOTH cases: the answer was cleared by the mid-loop arbiter and the boundary had no iteration left to apply it. ARCH-02 (2026-08-31): the first streak now MATERIALLY PROGRESSES - each round narrows the residual gap - so the three eligible audits (streaks 2, 3 and 4) all return DISTINCT_OR_MATERIALLY_PROGRESSING and change no route. That exhausts max_calls_per_mode=3, so the second streak is audited not at all and the existing full arbiter still runs at streaks 5 and 10, exactly as it did before ARCH-02. This fixture therefore remains the regression for two mid-loop rulings + a surviving human answer applied at the budget boundary, and additionally pins that an exhausted allowance preserves the existing route.
